scope: Inspect the public references requested for the preliminary FastChem comparison. Spectral calculations and metallicity retrieval are outside this task at the user's request.
inspection_note: Locations below identify the portions inspected, not a reproduction of each paper or its upstream measurements. Original PDFs, extracted article text and page images are not redistributed. Copy hashes identify downloaded bytes; web-reader-only sources have no byte hash.

sources.title: A Comparison of Chemical Models of Exoplanet Atmospheres Enabled by TauREx 3.1
sources.access: Published full-text PDF from the author's institutional repository; Table 1 also inspected on a rendered page.
findings: The published experiment uses a cloud-free, isothermal 1500 K HD 209458b analogue, solar metallicity and C/O=0.5, with simulated JWST uncertainties and unscattered spectra; 49 equilibrium and seven free-chemistry retrievals.

Matching elements and physical assumptions gives consistent posteriors despite different thermochemical implementations. The reported large biases concern mismatched elements or condensation. Matching elements does not mean identical molecular catalogs.
sources.application: Neither its bias magnitude nor its small matched-case differences quantify the effect of the present 2500-4000 K table comparison.

sources.title: Uncertainty quantification in thermochemistry, benchmarking electronic structure computations, and Active Thermochemical Tables
sources.access: Open-access publisher full-text HTML inspected with the web reader; direct local download returned HTTP 403.
sources.locations: Expression of uncertainties in thermochemistry; Type A and Type B uncertainties; Additional terms in the uncertainty; The role of benchmarks and their accuracy; Active Thermochemical Tables.
findings: Thermochemical uncertainties conventionally express estimated 95% confidence limits, approximately twice the standard deviation. Correlation changes uncertainty propagation.

Converting atomization energies to formation enthalpies requires atomic-reference uncertainties; conversion to 298.15 K also requires thermal increments. Spread among theoretical methods measures differences of biases, not their absolute uncertainty.
sources.application: Do not use table-to-table differences as independent Gaussian error bars.

sources.title: High-accuracy extrapolated ab initio thermochemistry. III. Additional improvements and overview
sources.access: Public author PDF inspected through the web reader's PDF text. Direct download returned HTTP 403 and page rendering was unavailable; no visual transcription audit is claimed.
sources.locations: Section II (p. 114111-2); Table I heading and HCN rows (pp. 114111-3 to 114111-4).
findings: Table I includes zero-point corrections: HCN HEAT-345QP atomization energy is 1268.59 kJ/mol. Its ATcT benchmark is 1268.26 +/- 0.17 kJ/mol from version 1.064, with 95% confidence limits.
sources.application: The historical benchmark is not ATcT 1.172. The current HCN provenance credits this calculation, so agreement with it is not independent validation of that network.

sources.title: Active Thermochemical Tables, Thermochemical Network version 1.172
sources.access: Official versioned HTML tables inspected with the web reader; direct local HCN download returned HTTP 403.
sources.locations: HCN summary, top contributors (TN 2754.4), correlated-species table and uncertainty footer; H and N summaries. C is also listed in the HCN correlation table.
findings: HCN Hf(298.15 K)=129.293 kJ/mol; displayed uncertainty +/-0.087 kJ/mol is an estimated 95% confidence limit. HCN and C have correlation 0.331.

The network lists HCN atomization 1268.59 +/-0.56 kJ/mol as a Harding 2008 input. This input uncertainty is the network's stated assessment. The top 20 contributors cover only 37.6% of HCN provenance.
sources.application: The selected correlations are not a complete covariance matrix. No correlated uncertainty propagation was performed.

sources.title: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, SRD 13
sources.access: Official numerical HTML tables; HCN response downloaded, atomic rows inspected with the web reader.
sources.locations: Headers and 0/298.15 K rows; HCN evaluation-date footer.
findings: HCN Hf(298.15 K)=135.143 kJ/mol. Standard pressure is 0.1 MPa (1 bar); the HCN evaluation is dated December 1969.
sources.application: Table values and conventions were checked, not the original experiments underlying the historical evaluation.

sources.title: Binding Energies in Atomic Negative Ions: III
sources.access: Public NIST full-text PDF; first page of Table 3 also inspected on a rendered page.
sources.locations: Sections 6-7 and Tables 3-4 (printed pp. 1526-1529; PDF pages 17-20).
findings: The compilation distinguishes neutral parent and anion states, selected electron affinities, bound excited terms, metastable states, and fine-structure intervals. Not every listed state is a stable ground-state anion.
sources.application: These distinctions matter when choosing a ground-state approximation or a partition sum. Reading the reference does not reconstruct Daniel's fitted coefficients or isolate the remaining anion differences.

hcn_energy_cross_check.basis: Derived from the selected public table entries and the existing offline adoption helper; no new equilibrium solve.
hcn_energy_cross_check.reaction: HCN -> H + C + N at 0 K
hcn_energy_cross_check.note: The existing helper uses Hf(298.15 K) + [H(0)-H(298.15 K)] in a common elemental reference gauge. The two rounded JANAF routes differ by 0.002 kJ/mol; the archived 0.06019568 eV shift uses the latter route. This is not an uncertainty estimate.

remaining_limits: The requested six references are accessible for the declared inspection scopes; no additional user-supplied copy is required for this review.
Full thermochemical-network reconstruction, complete covariance, the preliminary atomic-fit construction and independent whole-mixture validation remain unreviewed or unavailable.
Retrieved-metallicity effects and whole-mixture physical accuracy remain unknown. The historical controlled-cross-retrieval proposal is deferred and is not required to complete this task.
